resource_texts.fact_12: If the party pays Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter with chain mail and a shield, she will join them against the dragon. Her fee is unset, and she says she cannot kill the dragon herself; Sir Phidipaldi told her they would come back to hire her.

groups.basis: Both facts describe the same offer from beat_10: Lady Hilda will join the party against the dragon for pay. Each has the same trigger (hiring her) and the same benefit (a seasoned armored fighter for the dragon hunt). Both help thread_3 as established openings.
groups.text: If the party pays Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter with chain mail and a shield, she will join them against the dragon. Her fee is unset, and she says she cannot kill the dragon herself; Sir Phidipaldi told her they would come back to hire her.

rules.last_session: standalone beats rated low importance are dropped by code before assessment; threads/standalone events retain medium-or-high impact AND lasting consequence; an otherwise unrepresented encounter may also qualify with medium-or-high historical value, regardless of enduring consequence; no scene or character quota
rules.want: ongoing pursuit; adventure before side, then importance and actionability; serves_thread is null (an end, not a means) and significance is not incidental (Goals: parent_goal_id null, significance not incidental)
rules.owe: definite_end; commitment_type is not general_agreement; stake, burden and consequence are not trivial (Obligations filter)
rules.blocked_by: active, persists beyond the scene, not covered by immediate danger, and blocks a thread holding a shown want, debt or opening
rules.could_use: openings only; supported enabling action toward a shown want/debt; direct role; equivalent offers/plans use validated canonical fact references; assets stay in state/history
rules.unknown: question_type open_ended and all four dimensions medium or high (Mysteries filter)
rules.threat: harm_origin is not party and no evaluation is low (Brewing Troubles filter); not covered by an immediate danger
rules.all: never possibly moot facts; no caps; no assets in open matters

dropped_standalone.reason: Brandonsford has no real law enforcement, only a night watch, which is useful background but tied to no thread.
dropped_standalone.text: Brandonsford has no guards or proper law enforcement; a rotating group of able-bodied men keeps night watch, and an ancient small stone wall surrounds the town.

dropped_standalone.reason: The party gained entry to town; this was consequential but left nothing open.
dropped_standalone.text: When a night watchman challenged them, Sir Phidipaldi claimed the sacred law of Zeus for hospitality and Wayman said they came from Ithaca; the watchman let them in before nightfall and pointed out the two inns.

dropped_standalone.reason: The party learned the lodging terms at the Clumsy Fox.
dropped_standalone.text: The halfling owner Bentley gave Wayman a free first Fox Tail Brew, which tasted fantastic, and offered rooms at 10 silver a night; one gold would cover the whole party for multiple nights.
